acceptance_tests.evidence: test_U001-AT01 restores the same image id and queue context from a patch URL mounts App with the hash already set (a refresh), asserts getImage was called with img-42, then clicks Back and asserts the workbench URL still carries sort/filter/page and that the sort-select, filter-select and search-input controls read image_id / reviewed / 'case 3'. The same journey ran in real Chromium: deep link #/patch/Case-3-A17-15765-20926?sort=image_id&filter=unreviewed restored on reload and on a cold open in a new tab, and Back returned to #/workbench?sort=image_id&filter=unreviewed with both controls matching the URL.

test_U001-AT02 moves between screens exactly once per history step and removes its listener. It spies on addEventListener/removeEventListener, records every hashchange listener, walks workbench -> patch -> workbench, and asserts the workbench fetched exactly once more for the single Back step (a second listener would setRoute twice and refetch). After unmount it asserts removed equals added, so nothing leaks. The count is of workbench-shaped fetches only: PatchReview separately lists images on mount to build its prev/next queue, and counting those too would have conflated the two screens.

test_U001-AT03 round-trips eight ids through serializeRoute/parseRoute - 'img-1', 'a b', 'a/b', 'a#b?c=d&e', '100%', 'cafe-9', '../../etc/passwd', 'a+b=c&d' - asserting each comes back byte-identical and that no unencoded ? or # survives in the path segment. Decoding happens after splitting, so an id containing / survives. A boundary sweep of the module outside the test harness added emoji, a 500-char id and percent-encoded traversal, all stable.

test_U001-AT04 shows a meaningful view instead of an empty screen for unknown routes, over #/analytics, #/nope/deep/path and #/patch/: each renders data-testid=route-unavailable with non-empty text matching /not available/i, and the disclaimer still renders, so it is not a blank page. Confirmed in Chromium for #/analytics. The five declared-but-unimplemented routes of the brief's union and any unrecognized path both land here, distinguished by the `declared` flag.

test_U001-AT05 keeps tokens and review notes out of the URL: it types 'dx: invasive carcinoma, block A3' into the review note, navigates, and asserts the href matches neither that text nor /token|bearer|authorization|api[_-]?key|session=/i, and that every query key present is one of sort/filter/q/page. A module-level test smuggles token, review_note and patient_id onto a route object and asserts none reaches the hash - the serializer builds its string from known fields, so there is no pass-through path at all.

limitations: The skip link is a real, focusable control that moves focus to <main id=main-content>, but it has no visual treatment: hiding it until focused needs one rule in app/g6/frontend/src/styles.css, which is outside this task's section 5 surface. Flagged rather than worked around.

PatchReview builds its prev/next queue from a hardcoded listImages({sort: priority, filter: all, page: 1}) and ignores the queue context the patch route now carries. Pre-existing behavior, unchanged by U001, and left alone because fixing it would change patch navigation.

Queue context is stored in the URL, so a pasted link reveals the reviewer's current filter and search text. That is navigation context by design (section 8 step 3), and search text is capped at 200 characters with control characters stripped. It is not a reviewer note or a patient identifier; if search terms must not travel in links, that is a product decision for the integrator.

Only implemented destinations appear in the nav. overview, source-groups, analytics, system and demo parse as declared routes and show the not-available view, so deep links to them are honest rather than blank.

boundary_observations: A sweep of navigation.ts outside the test harness (19 hostile inputs: emoji, a 500-char id, percent-encoded traversal, duplicate and out-of-range page keys, __proto__/constructor in the query, control characters, a 5,000-character search term, a 300-segment path, case-mismatched route names) produced 0 throws and 0 unstable parse/serialize round trips, and confirmed: no prototype pollution, search text capped at 200, control characters stripped, unknown keys ignored, and page=1e308 / Infinity / 1.5 / 0 / -3 / duplicates all falling back to 1. Because a URL can now carry an arbitrary image id where ids previously came only from the server, the api.ts path construction was checked rather than assumed: getImage and every sibling encodeURIComponent the id, so a traversal-shaped id is inert.
